# Acme Health Information Security Standard: AI Governance & Accountability

**Standard ID:** STD-AIGOV-001
**Owner (end to end):** AI Risk / GRC
**Applies to:** All Acme Health personnel, teams, and partners who design, develop, deploy, evaluate, procure, use, oversee, or decommission AI systems.
**Audience:** Acme Health security, IT, risk, compliance, and engineering staff who implement and audit against this document.

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This Standard establishes Acme Health's requirements for governing and accounting for artificial intelligence (AI) systems across their lifecycle. AI Risk / GRC is accountable for this process end to end, including its handoffs to other participating teams. Other teams (e.g., Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Clinical Operations, Executive Leadership) participate in individual steps as specified below, but AI Risk / GRC owns the process and answers for its outcome.

## 2. Legal and Regulatory Requirements for AI

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.1]

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Govern 1.1, maintaining awareness of the applicable legal and regulatory considerations and requirements specific to industry, sector, and business purpose, as well as the application context of the deployed AI system (Action 1); aligning risk management efforts with applicable legal standards (Action 2); and maintaining policies for training and re-training organizational staff about necessary legal or regulatory considerations that may impact AI-related design, development, and deployment activities (Action 3). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.1 Action 1 | Govern 1.1 Action 2 | Govern 1.1 Action 3]

## 3. Trustworthy AI in Organizational Policies

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that the characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into Acme Health's organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.2]

NIST suggests, among its 15 actions for Govern 1.2, defining key terms and concepts related to AI systems and the scope of their purposes and intended uses (Action 1); connecting AI governance to existing organizational governance and risk controls (Action 2); aligning to broader data governance policies and practices, particularly the use of sensitive or otherwise risky data (Action 3); detailing standards for experimental design, data quality, and model training (Action 4); outlining and documenting risk mapping and measurement processes and standards (Action 5); detailing model testing and validation processes (Action 6); detailing review processes for legal and risk functions (Action 7); establishing the frequency of and detail for monitoring, auditing, and review processes (Action 8); outlining change management requirements (Action 9); outlining processes for internal and external stakeholder engagement (Action 10); establishing whistleblower policies to facilitate reporting of serious AI system concerns (Action 11); detailing and testing incident response plans (Action 12); verifying that formal AI risk management policies align to existing legal standards and industry best practices and norms (Action 13); establishing AI risk management policies that broadly align to AI system trustworthy characteristics (Action 14); and verifying that formal AI risk management policies include currently deployed and third-party AI systems (Action 15). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.2 Action 1 | Govern 1.2 Action 2 | Govern 1.2 Action 3 | Govern 1.2 Action 4 | Govern 1.2 Action 5 | Govern 1.2 Action 6 | Govern 1.2 Action 7 | Govern 1.2 Action 8 | Govern 1.2 Action 9 | Govern 1.2 Action 10 | Govern 1.2 Action 11 | Govern 1.2 Action 12 | Govern 1.2 Action 13 | Govern 1.2 Action 14 | Govern 1.2 Action 15]

## 4. Risk Tolerance and Required Level of Risk Management

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain processes, procedures, and practices to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.3]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 1.3, establishing policies to define mechanisms for measuring or understanding an AI system's potential impacts, for example via regular impact assessments at key stages in the AI lifecycle connected to system impacts and frequency of system updates (Action 1); establishing policies to define mechanisms for measuring or understanding the likelihood of an AI system's impacts and their magnitude at key stages in the AI lifecycle (Action 2); establishing policies that define assessment scales for measuring potential AI system impact, which may be qualitative such as red-amber-green (RAG) or may entail simulations or econometric approaches (Action 3); establishing policies for assigning an overall risk measurement approach for an AI system or its important components, for example via multiplication or combination of a mapped risk's impact and likelihood (Action 4); and establishing policies to assign systems to uniform risk scales that are valid across the organization's AI portfolio, acknowledging that risk tolerance and risk levels may change over the lifecycle of an AI system (Action 5). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.3 Action 1 | Govern 1.3 Action 2 | Govern 1.3 Action 3 | Govern 1.3 Action 4 | Govern 1.3 Action 5]

## 5. Transparent Risk Management Process and Documentation

AI Risk / GRC shall establish the risk management process and its outcomes through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.4]

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Govern 1.4, establishing and regularly reviewing documentation policies addressing information such as AI actor contact information, business justification, scope and usages, expected and potential risks and impacts, assumptions and limitations, description and characterization of training data, algorithmic methodology, evaluated alternative approaches, description of output data, testing and validation results, down- and up-stream dependencies, plans for deployment, monitoring, and change management, and stakeholder engagement plans (Action 1); verifying that documentation policies for AI systems are standardized across the organization and remain current (Action 2); establishing policies for a model documentation inventory system and regularly reviewing its completeness, usability, and efficacy (Action 3); establishing mechanisms to regularly review the efficacy of risk management processes (Action 4); identifying AI actors responsible for evaluating efficacy of risk management processes and approaches and for course-correction based on results (Action 5); establishing policies and processes regarding public disclosure of the use of AI and risk management material such as impact assessments, audits, model documentation, and validation and testing results (Action 6); and documenting and reviewing the use and efficacy of different types of transparency tools and following industry standards at the time a model is in use (Action 7). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.4 Action 1 | Govern 1.4 Action 2 | Govern 1.4 Action 3 | Govern 1.4 Action 4 | Govern 1.4 Action 5 | Govern 1.4 Action 6 | Govern 1.4 Action 7]

## 6. Monitoring and Periodic Review of the Risk Management Process

AI Risk / GRC shall plan ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes, shall clearly define organizational roles and responsibilities for those activities, and shall determine the frequency of periodic review ([Review Frequency]). [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.5]

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Govern 1.5, establishing policies to allocate appropriate resources and capacity for assessing impacts of AI systems on individuals, communities, and society (Action 1); establishing policies and procedures for monitoring and addressing AI system performance and trustworthiness, including bias and security problems, across the lifecycle of the system (Action 2); establishing policies for AI system incident response, or confirming that existing incident response policies apply to AI systems (Action 3); establishing policies to define organizational functions and personnel responsible for AI system monitoring and incident response activities (Action 4); establishing mechanisms to enable the sharing of feedback from impacted individuals or communities about negative impacts from AI systems (Action 5); establishing mechanisms to provide recourse for impacted individuals or communities to contest problematic AI system outcomes (Action 6); and establishing opt-out mechanisms (Action 7). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.5 Action 1 | Govern 1.5 Action 2 | Govern 1.5 Action 3 | Govern 1.5 Action 4 | Govern 1.5 Action 5 | Govern 1.5 Action 6 | Govern 1.5 Action 7]

## 7. AI System Inventory

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain mechanisms to inventory AI systems, and shall resource those mechanisms according to organizational risk priorities. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.6]

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 1.6, establishing policies that define the creation and maintenance of AI system inventories (Action 1); establishing policies that define a specific individual or team that is responsible for maintaining the inventory (Action 2); establishing policies that define which models or systems are inventoried, with preference to inventorying all models or systems or, minimally, high risk models or systems, or systems deployed in high-stakes settings (Action 3); and establishing policies that define model or system attributes to be inventoried, for example documentation, links to source code, incident response plans, data dictionaries, and AI actor contact information (Action 4). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.6 Action 1 | Govern 1.6 Action 2 | Govern 1.6 Action 3 | Govern 1.6 Action 4]

## 8. Decommissioning and Phase-Out of AI Systems

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain processes and procedures for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization's trustworthiness. [NIST AI RMF Govern 1.7]

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 1.7, establishing policies for decommissioning AI systems that typically address user and community concerns and reputational risks, business continuity and financial risks, up- and downstream system dependencies, regulatory requirements such as data retention, potential future legal, regulatory, security, or forensic investigations, and migration to the replacement system if appropriate (Action 1); establishing policies that delineate where and for how long decommissioned systems, models, and related artifacts are stored (Action 2); establishing practices to track accountability and consider how decommission and other adaptations or changes in system deployment contribute to downstream impacts for individuals, groups, and communities (Action 3); and establishing policies that address ancillary data or artifacts that must be preserved for fulsome understanding or execution of the decommissioned AI system, for example predictions, explanations, intermediate input feature representations, and usernames and passwords (Action 4). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.7 Action 1 | Govern 1.7 Action 2 | Govern 1.7 Action 3 | Govern 1.7 Action 4]

## 9. Roles, Responsibilities, and Lines of Communication

AI Risk / GRC shall document roles, responsibilities, and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks, and shall ensure they are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization. [NIST AI RMF Govern 2.1]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Govern 2.1, establishing policies that define the AI risk management roles and responsibilities for positions directly and indirectly related to AI systems, including but not limited to boards of directors or advisory committees, senior management, AI audit functions, product management, project management, AI design, AI development, human-AI interaction, AI testing and evaluation, AI acquisition and procurement, impact assessment functions, and oversight functions (Action 1); establishing policies that promote regular communication among AI actors participating in AI risk management efforts (Action 2); establishing policies that separate management of AI system development functions from AI system testing functions to enable independent course-correction of AI systems (Action 3); establishing policies to identify, increase the transparency of, and prevent conflicts of interest in AI risk management efforts (Action 4); establishing policies to counteract confirmation bias and market incentives that may hinder AI risk management efforts (Action 5); and establishing policies that incentivize AI actors to collaborate with existing legal, oversight, compliance, or enterprise risk functions in their AI risk management activities (Action 6). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.1 Action 1 | Govern 2.1 Action 2 | Govern 2.1 Action 3 | Govern 2.1 Action 4 | Govern 2.1 Action 5 | Govern 2.1 Action 6]

## 10. AI Risk Management Training

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that the organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements. [NIST AI RMF Govern 2.2]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Govern 2.2, establishing policies for personnel addressing ongoing education about applicable laws and regulations for AI systems, potential negative impacts that may arise from AI systems, organizational AI policies, and trustworthy AI characteristics (Action 1); ensuring that trainings are suitable across AI actor sub-groups, for AI actors carrying out technical tasks such as developers and operators as compared to AI actors in oversight roles such as legal, compliance, and audit (Action 2); ensuring that trainings comprehensively address technical and socio-technical aspects of AI risk management (Action 3); verifying that organizational AI policies include mechanisms for internal AI personnel to acknowledge and commit to their roles and responsibilities (Action 4); verifying that organizational policies address change management and include mechanisms to communicate and acknowledge substantial AI system changes (Action 5); and defining paths along internal and external chains of accountability to escalate risk concerns (Action 6). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.2 Action 1 | Govern 2.2 Action 2 | Govern 2.2 Action 3 | Govern 2.2 Action 4 | Govern 2.2 Action 5 | Govern 2.2 Action 6]

## 11. Executive Accountability for AI Risk Decisions

Acme Health executive leadership shall take responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment. [NIST AI RMF Govern 2.3]

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Govern 2.3, that organizational management declare risk tolerances for developing or using AI systems, support AI risk management efforts and play an active role in such efforts, integrate a risk and harm prevention mindset throughout the AI lifecycle as part of organizational culture, support competent risk management executives, and delegate the power, resources, and authorization to perform risk management to each appropriate level throughout the management chain (Action 1); and that organizations establish board committees for AI risk management and oversight functions and integrate those functions within the organization's broader enterprise risk management approaches (Action 2). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.3 Action 1 | Govern 2.3 Action 2]

## 12. Diverse Decision-Making

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team, including diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds. [NIST AI RMF Govern 3.1]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 3.1, defining policies and hiring practices at the outset that promote interdisciplinary roles, competencies, skills, and capacity for AI efforts (Action 1); defining policies and hiring practices that lead to demographic and domain expertise diversity, empowering staff with necessary resources and support, and facilitating the contribution of staff feedback and concerns without fear of reprisal (Action 2); establishing policies that facilitate inclusivity and the integration of new insights into existing practice (Action 3); seeking external expertise to supplement organizational diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility where internal expertise is lacking (Action 4); and establishing policies that incentivize AI actors to collaborate with existing nondiscrimination, accessibility and accommodation, and human resource functions, employee resource groups (ERGs), and diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) initiatives (Action 5). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 3.1 Action 1 | Govern 3.1 Action 2 | Govern 3.1 Action 3 | Govern 3.1 Action 4 | Govern 3.1 Action 5]

## 13. Human-AI Configurations and Oversight of AI Systems

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain policies and procedures that define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems. [NIST AI RMF Govern 3.2]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Govern 3.2, establishing policies and procedures that define and differentiate the various human roles and responsibilities when using, interacting with, or monitoring AI systems (Action 1); establishing procedures for capturing and tracking risk information related to human-AI configurations and associated outcomes (Action 2); establishing policies for the development of proficiency standards for AI actors carrying out system operation tasks and system oversight tasks (Action 3); establishing specified risk management training protocols for AI actors carrying out system operation tasks and system oversight tasks (Action 4); establishing policies and procedures regarding AI actor roles and responsibilities for human oversight of deployed systems (Action 5); establishing policies and procedures defining human-AI configurations, meaning configurations where AI systems are explicitly designated and treated as team members in primarily human teams, in relation to organizational risk tolerances and associated documentation (Action 6); establishing policies to enhance the explanation, interpretation, and overall transparency of AI systems (Action 7); and establishing policies for managing risks regarding known difficulties in human-AI configurations, human-AI teaming, and AI system user experience and user interactions (UI/UX) (Action 8). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 3.2 Action 1 | Govern 3.2 Action 2 | Govern 3.2 Action 3 | Govern 3.2 Action 4 | Govern 3.2 Action 5 | Govern 3.2 Action 6 | Govern 3.2 Action 7 | Govern 3.2 Action 8]

## 14. Critical Thinking and Safety-First Mindset

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational policies and practices that foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts. [NIST AI RMF Govern 4.1]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 4.1, establishing policies that require inclusion of oversight functions — legal, compliance, and risk management — from the outset of the system design process (Action 1); establishing policies that promote effective challenge of AI system design, implementation, and deployment decisions via mechanisms such as the three lines of defense, model audits, or red-teaming, to minimize workplace risks such as groupthink (Action 2); establishing policies that incentivize safety-first mindset and general critical thinking and review at an organizational and procedural level (Action 3); establishing whistleblower protections for insiders who report on perceived serious problems with AI systems (Action 4); and establishing policies to integrate a harm and risk prevention mindset throughout the AI lifecycle (Action 5). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.1 Action 1 | Govern 4.1 Action 2 | Govern 4.1 Action 3 | Govern 4.1 Action 4 | Govern 4.1 Action 5]

## 15. Documentation and Communication of AI Risks and Impacts

Organizational teams that design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use AI technology shall document the risks and potential impacts of that technology, and shall communicate about those impacts more broadly; AI Risk / GRC owns and accounts for this documentation and communication process end to end. [NIST AI RMF Govern 4.2]

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 4.2, establishing impact assessment policies and processes for AI systems used by the organization (Action 1); aligning organizational impact assessment activities with relevant regulatory or legal requirements (Action 2); verifying that impact assessment activities are appropriate to evaluate the potential negative impact of a system and how quickly a system changes, and that assessments are applied on a regular basis (Action 3); and utilizing impact assessments to inform broader evaluations of AI system risk (Action 4). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.2 Action 1 | Govern 4.2 Action 2 | Govern 4.2 Action 3 | Govern 4.2 Action 4]

## 16. AI Testing, Incident Identification, and Information Sharing

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational practices that enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing. [NIST AI RMF Govern 4.3]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 4.3, establishing policies and procedures to facilitate and equip AI system testing (Action 1); establishing organizational commitment to identifying AI system limitations and sharing of insights about limitations within appropriate AI actor groups (Action 2); establishing policies for reporting and documenting incident response (Action 3); establishing policies and processes regarding public disclosure of incidents and information sharing (Action 4); and establishing guidelines for incident handling related to AI system risks and performance (Action 5). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.3 Action 1 | Govern 4.3 Action 2 | Govern 4.3 Action 3 | Govern 4.3 Action 4 | Govern 4.3 Action 5]

## 17. External Feedback on AI Impacts

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational policies and practices to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks. [NIST AI RMF Govern 5.1]

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Govern 5.1, establishing AI risk management policies that explicitly address mechanisms for collecting, evaluating, and incorporating stakeholder and user feedback that could include recourse mechanisms for faulty AI system outputs, bug bounties, human-centered design, user-interaction and experience research, and participatory stakeholder engagement with individuals and communities that may experience negative impacts (Action 1); verifying that stakeholder feedback is considered and addressed, including environmental concerns and across the entire population of intended users, including historically excluded populations, people with disabilities, older people, and those with limited access to the internet and other basic technologies (Action 2); and clarifying the organization's principles as they apply to AI systems, considering those which have been proposed publicly, to inform external stakeholders of the organization's values, and considering publishing or adopting AI principles (Action 3). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 5.1 Action 1 | Govern 5.1 Action 2 | Govern 5.1 Action 3]

## 18. Incorporation of Adjudicated Feedback into System Design and Implementation

AI Risk / GRC shall establish mechanisms that enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation. [NIST AI RMF Govern 5.2]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 5.2, explicitly acknowledging that AI systems and the use of AI present inherent costs and risks along with potential benefits (Action 1); defining reasonable risk tolerances for AI systems informed by laws, regulation, best practices, or industry standards (Action 2); establishing policies that ensure all relevant AI actors are provided with meaningful opportunities to provide feedback on system design and implementation (Action 3); establishing policies that define how to assign AI systems to established risk tolerance levels by combining system impact assessments with the likelihood that an impact occurs, often entailing some combination of econometric evaluations of impacts and impact likelihoods, red-amber-green (RAG) scales for impact severity and likelihood, policies for allocating risk management resources along established risk tolerance levels with higher-risk systems receiving more risk management resources and oversight, and policies for approval, conditional approval, and disapproval of the design, implementation, and deployment of AI systems (Action 4); and establishing policies facilitating the early decommissioning of AI systems that surpass an organization's ability to reasonably mitigate risks (Action 5). [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 5.2 Action 1 | Govern 5.2 Action 2 | Govern 5.2 Action 3 | Govern 5.2 Action 4 | Govern 5.2 Action 5]

## 19. Compliance and Enforcement

Compliance with this Standard is audited by AI Risk / GRC, which owns this process end to end and answers for its outcome. Deviations shall be reported to AI Risk / GRC and tracked to resolution. The "NIST suggests" statements in this document reflect NIST's voluntary suggested actions from the NIST AI RMF Playbook and are not requirements of Acme Health; the tagged requirement statements in Sections 2 through 18 are binding on the personnel and teams to whom they are addressed.
